why: Build for pipe plumbing in next/, on main with experiment 295 merged in. The ledger turn gains end(stream), max(pos) by the (stream, pos) index, one row always, so the older T936 reads law stays flat at an empty inbox. Program mail checks the cap after the saved receipt and answers full with nothing saved; ProcessManager.ack writes the reader's ack on processes/<name>/acked, forward only and only from the live life. The runner acks after each checkpoint save and again at a turn's start, a lost ack failing no turn; a plain send folds full; send_chunks cuts with the size kept on its dispatched entry, delivers part seq under <cmd id>/part/<seq>, waits owed on full, and a later send or send_chunks to the same name waits behind it. Waiting behind any owed plain send broke the existing M2 alarm law, so only a waiting send_chunks holds mail back. mail.unread (256, 1 to 16,384) and mail.chunk (64 KiB, 1 KiB to 1 MiB) are repo settings handed in by the cloud runtime, which also carries full and processAck; the Project object class gains processAck.
